To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
corticofugal neurons in S1 cortex facilitate the somatosensory responses of ventrobasal neurons in the rat thalamus.

1) the corticofugal projections from S1 to VB thalami of the awake rat facilitate the responses of VB neurons to electrical stimuli of the medial lemniscal pathway; and 2) the facilitation is not attributable to the activation of subthalamically located corticofugal neurons.

the responses of 66% of ventrobasal neurons in the awake, freely behaving rat to repetitive stimulation of the medial lemniscal pathway are reduced when the primary somatosensory (S1) cortex is suppressed.

the mechanisms of cortical plasticity.

the role of the cerebral cortex in the processing of information from the somatosensory system in the awake rat and the effects of sensory experience on the development of cortical and subcortical somatosensory neurons.
the role of the cerebral cortex in the processing of information about the somatic environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the corticofugal system in the rat has a net facilitatory influence on thalamic relay neurons.
corticofugal effects on the somatosensory system in the rat are not consistent.

, in the rat, S1 cortical neurons exert a facilitatory effect on VB thalamic responses to somatic stimuli, whereas S1 cortical suppression has little effect on thalamic responses evoked by medial lemniscal stimuli.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
corticofugal neurons are not essential for normal transmission of somatosensory information through the lemniscal pathway, but they do enhance transmission of this information.
corticofugal facilitation of sensory transmission is a general phenomenon in the mammalian brain.
corticothalamic influences are facilitatory and corticofugal projections are inhibitory.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the S1 cortex is the main source of facilitatory input to the ventrobasal nuclei in the awake rat.
, in the conscious rat, corticothalamic feedback facilitates sensory transmission from the periphery through the thalamus to cortex.
corticofugal projections are a major contributor to the processing of somatosensory information in thalamus.
